newsitem.title: NORWAY: Kvaerner in 5 bln NOK UK road deal.
newsitem.headline: Kvaerner in 5 bln NOK UK road deal.

text.p: Midland Expressway Ltd, which is 50 percent owned by anglo-Norwegian group Kvaerner ASA and Italy's Autostrade, has won a British road construction contract worth five billion crowns ($655.9 million), Kvaerner said on Monday.
Kvaerner said in a statement that Midland Expressway had been given British government approval to build Britain's first toll motorway, the privately funded Birmingham Northern Relief Road.

"Midland Expressway, which is owned equally by Kvaerner and Autostrade, the leading operator of tolled motorways in Europe, entered into a 53-year concession agreement with the UK Government to design, finance, build and operate the 43.5 kilometre Birmingham Northern Relief Road (BNRR) in February 1992," Kvaerner said.
"Today's go-ahead for the BNRR follows one of the most detailed and extensive Public Inquiries for any comparable road scheme in Britain," the statement said.
When completed, the BNRR will provide an alternative through-route in the heavily congested West Midlands M6 corridor, the vital link between London and the south east, and the north west of England.
The section of existing motorway through the West Midlands regularly carries more than 150,000 vehicles per day - on a route designed to take half that number, Kvaerner said.
